title: When the Thera (Santorini) volcano erupted
summary: Radiocarbon dates for the eruption run about a century older than archaeological dates; a 2020 recalibration narrowed the gap, but the exact year is not settled.
why: The date is a fixed point for building Bronze Age timelines in the Aegean.

notes.problem: Range omitted the 1627-1600 BCE olive-branch date it cites; source says IntCal20 'mitigates' the disagreement.

question: When exactly did the Minoan eruption of Thera happen?
wouldSettle: A precisely dated tree-ring or ice-core marker tied to Thera ash.

theories.name: Radiocarbon high date
theories.idea: Radiocarbon puts the eruption in the late 17th or 16th century BCE.

theories.name: Archaeological low date
theories.idea: Archaeological dating places it about 1550–1480 BCE.
